name: C-K Plastics, Inc.
old_description: A leading manufacturer of custom thermoplastic extruded, injection molded and blow molded plastic parts since 1978.
about:
C-K Plastics, Inc. operates from St. Louis, Missouri, where it was founded in 1978. The company was acquired by Technical Industries in 2011 and continues to operate as a manufacturer of custom thermoplastic parts. From its start, the firm focused on challenging products that other manufacturers avoided, such as large-diameter profile extrusions and complex blow-molded shapes requiring specialized tooling.

The company produces custom extruded profiles, tubing, blow-molded parts (up to 2-pound shot sizes), and precision injection-molded components using filled and unfilled engineered resins. An in-house tool shop controls tooling design and fabrication, and the facility offers engineering assistance, material selection guidance, secondary fabrication, assembly, and special packaging. No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

C-K Plastics serves a broad range of industries with custom and specialty extrusions, though the company does not name specific sectors in its public materials. Customers include those needing low-volume or challenging geometries that standard suppliers decline.

The firm emphasizes its willingness to take on difficult projects, continuous technology adoption, and a quality system certified to ISO 2001:2015 (2018). A quality database supports 3 Sigma and 6 Sigma capability reporting, and cost-mitigation programs include dock-to-stock qualification, pull systems, and just-in-time delivery.

name: C.R. International Inc.
old_description: Providing our customers with quality electronic manufacturing services for over 40 years!
about:
C.R. International Inc., headquartered in Laurel, Maryland, was founded in 1981 as a small engineering firm supplying communications and data-processing equipment to federal customers. The company is a certified Woman-Owned Small Business and has remained independently owned since its inception.

Today CRI operates as a full-service electronic manufacturing services (EMS) provider. Its capabilities span printed circuit board assembly, surface-mount technology on two SMT lines equipped with DEK screen printers and Mycronic pick-and-place machines capable of placing 01005 components through large BGAs, conformal coating in acrylic, silicone, or epoxy, box-build and electro-mechanical integration, and functional testing. Production takes place in an 18,000-square-foot climate-controlled facility that supports prototype through volume runs.

The customer base includes military, aerospace and flight, communications, industrial, and Department of Defense programs, as well as start-ups. The company cites NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory and defense prime contractors as references, highlighting work on flight-certified hardware and mission-critical defense electronics.

CRI positions itself as a partner rather than a vendor, stressing flexibility, responsiveness, and a commitment to the highest standards of ethics and quality. Its quality system is built around IPC Class III workmanship, ITAR compliance, and CMMC Level 2 cybersecurity certification.

name: CAMM Metals, Inc.
old_description: At CAMM Metals, our team specializes in MIG and TIG welding techniques. Whether working with steel, stainless steel, or aluminum, our skilled welders ensure precise and durable welds that meet the highest quality standards.
about:
CAMM Metals, Inc. was founded in 1996 by Al Soucie in his household garage in East Windsor, Connecticut. The company, named for his family members Craig, Al, Marge, and Matt, began as a one-man operation with an iron worker and a kerosene heater. By 1997 it moved into a 3,000‑square‑foot building, and today it operates as a second‑generation, family‑owned job shop from a 17,000‑square‑foot facility in the same town.

The shop provides full‑service sheet metal fabrication, including laser cutting, laser tube cutting, water jet cutting, MIG and TIG welding, CNC machining, and 3D printing. It handles small lots and batch runs up to 10,000 pieces, producing small‑ to medium‑sized fabrications, weldments, and OEM equipment for industrial customers. The plant is ISO 9001 certified and runs on CAD‑driven equipment designed for tight tolerances and intricate geometries.

CAMM Metals serves OEMs across New England and New York State, supporting a broad range of industries since 1996. Its customer base includes manufacturers requiring precision metal parts in steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, plastics, and exotic alloys such as Inconel and titanium.

The company emphasizes continuous improvement, reinvesting profits into new technology and cloud‑based workflow tools to shorten lead times and improve quality. Its single‑source model covers cutting, bending, fabricating, and welding, aiming to deliver high‑quality metal parts on schedule.

name: CED Central Ohio
old_description: We are regarded as one of the top electrical suppliers in the Columbus Ohio region. From Mansfield to Cincinnati and everywhere in-between. With locations in Columbus and Newark we are poised to help you grow your business.
about:
CED Central Ohio operates as a branch of Consolidated Electrical Distributors (CED), a national network with more than 700 locations across the United States. The company serves the Columbus, Ohio region from two facilities in Columbus and Newark, covering a service area that stretches from Mansfield to Cincinnati and includes Franklin, Licking, Delaware, Fairfield, and surrounding counties.

The branch stocks a broad line of residential, commercial, and industrial electrical products from manufacturers such as Square D (Schneider Electric), Southwire, Milwaukee Tool, Acuity Brands, Leviton, Sylvania, and Cooper Lighting Solutions. Beyond product distribution, it provides asset management solutions, customer project storage, switchgear quotations and project management, design-build services, lighting design and quotations, and a local delivery fleet.

Its customer base includes commercial electrical contractors, residential electrical contractors, multi-family developers, industrial facilities, utilities, and national accounts. The company positions itself as a full-line electrical supply partner for projects ranging from residential renovations to large-scale commercial and industrial installations.

CED Central Ohio emphasizes a policy of service, integrity, and reliability, citing its local inventory depth, dedicated sales team, and delivery capabilities as key differentiators in the Columbus market.

old_description: Manufacturing innovation and technology have never moved faster, and finding answers to today's challenges can be difficult. With a local teammate bringing solutions and products right to your door, you can find the answers you need to help you reach your goals and succeed.
about:
Columbia Electric Supply, operating as CES Idaho Falls, is based in Idaho Falls, Idaho. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founder names. It positions itself as a local teammate for industrial customers in the region.

CES does not manufacture products; rather, it distributes and integrates industrial automation hardware, software, and services. Its portfolio includes Rockwell Automation motor control equipment such as the M100 line, Grace Technologies' ChekVolt voltage indicators, and the FactoryXT suite for smart manufacturing. The firm provides solution consulting, system integration, industrial network consulting, and training programs with pre-built learning pathways.

The company serves industries including water and wastewater treatment, food and beverage processing, timber, and energy. Customers range from facility operators needing safety and efficiency upgrades to plants pursuing digital transformation of data, processes, and people.

CES emphasizes its role as an integrated partner that brings solutions and products directly to the customer's door, combining local presence with access to national automation brands. Its FactoryXT team is dedicated to connecting and digitizing manufacturing operations using current software and hardware.

name: CI Sport
old_description: CI Sport holds over 300 collegiate licenses and wants to work with you! We offer the latest styles of garments and unique designs.
about:
CI Sport traces its roots to Fargo, North Dakota, where in the late 1980s entrepreneurs Randy Thorson and Warren Ackley launched a screen-printing startup to supply decorated uniforms and souvenirs to local bars and restaurants. The business formally established its corporate division, CI Apparel, in 1990 and has since grown into a national supplier of licensed and custom-decorated apparel.

Today the company operates three divisions—CI Sport for collegiate licensed goods, CI Apparel for custom corporate wear, and CI Tourism for resort and tourism designs—from a 73,000-square-foot facility in southwest Fargo that opened in 2020. The plant houses all decoration production in-house, including embroidery (12-piece minimum, over 1,000 thread colors) and screen printing (36-piece minimum, PMS color matching), plus digitizing, art creation, inventory management, and e-commerce fulfillment for more than 25 online clients. The company also installs concept shops and t-shirt towers that serve over 700 college bookstores across 49 states.

Its customer base spans collegiate retail (bookstores, arenas, sporting-goods stores), professional sports leagues such as the NHL and NBA, minor-league baseball and hockey venues, corporate clients across virtually every industry, and tourism operators. CI Sport holds more than 300 collegiate licenses and works with major licensing companies, while also distributing brands like Nike, OGIO, and Columbia.

The founders started the business to meet a hospitality-industry need for decorated uniforms, and the company says its differentiating factor is the rare complete in-house facility that controls every step from art to finished goods. Low minimum orders (12–24 pieces depending on division) and fast turnaround times are cited as key advantages for corporate and tourism accounts.

about:
CK12 Designs operates from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, where it produces custom handcrafted furniture. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but it emphasizes local employment, hiring Oklahomans to build each piece.

The shop specializes in modern industrial farmhouse designs, crafting items such as beam consoles, charcuterie boards, coffee tables, dining tables, entertainment consoles, mantels, and custom live‑edged tables. All pieces are built from solid recycled wood sourced from native Oklahoma trees that have died naturally, been removed by homeowners, or salvaged from warehouse demolitions; no particle board is used.

CK12 Designs sells directly to residential customers through its website, serving homeowners seeking one‑of‑a‑kind furniture and reclaimed lumber for personal projects.

The company states that its custom-made furniture is frequently less expensive than pre‑fabricated alternatives from large retailers, and it differentiates itself by using only solid reclaimed wood and local labor.
